title: Outflare
description: Requests, job queue, Postgres and process health for an Outflare server. See docs/monitoring.md in outflareai/outflare.

panels.title: Requests refused by rate limits
panels.description: 429s by limit: api (per token), register, site_ip (unknown site keys), site_key (per key), site_visitor (per visitor behind a site's proxy).

panels.title: Jobs due, by kind
panels.description: Jobs whose run_at has passed, waiting for a worker.

panels.title: Wait before a worker picks a job up (p95)
Jobs put back after their lease ran out
panels.description: Running jobs requeued because their worker stopped holding them (a crash, or a process killed before its shutdown grace ended). Each may run twice. Normal is none: a deploy hands its jobs back at once (outcome interrupted or released on the jobs panel).

panels.title: Time waiting for a connection
panels.description: Above zero means the pool is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Below 99% means the working set no longer fits in memory.

panels.title: Sequential scans on large tables
panels.description: A large table scanned often is missing an index.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Cores in use.

panels.title: Oldest due item, by stage (the bottleneck)
panels.description: How long the longest-waiting item of each stage has waited for a worker. The highest line is the bottleneck: give that stage more workers, or find what it waits on below.

panels.title: Items due, by stage
panels.description: Items ready and waiting for a worker. A line that keeps growing is a stage that can't keep up.

panels.title: Items finished, by outcome
panels.description: What stages decided per second, across every worker.

panels.title: Why items stop
panels.description: Error and reason codes per second, by stage: rate limits, provider errors, AI failures, budget pauses, skips.

panels.title: Batch time (p95), by stage
panels.description: How long one batch takes. A slow stage with a small backlog is fine; a slow stage with a growing backlog needs more workers or a faster provider.

panels.title: Wait before a worker picks an item up (p95)
panels.description: Time from an item being due to being claimed, by stage.

panels.title: Calls held back by limits
panels.description: Calls to outside accounts that waited: rate is a rate limit, breaker is an account paused after repeated failures, probe is waiting for the one test call.

panels.title: Outside accounts: call outcomes and open breakers
panels.description: Calls by outcome per second, and accounts whose breaker is open now.

panels.title: Runs, by state
panels.description: Runs running or paused. Many paused runs usually means workspaces hit a budget or lost a connection.

panels.title: Items in progress and held
panels.description: Items claimed by workers, and items waiting for a person.

panels.title: AI calls by tool
panels.description: AI model calls booked per minute, by tool. Every call runs on the workspace's own key.

panels.title: AI spend by tool (US$ per hour)
panels.description: What AI calls cost on workspaces' own provider bills, by tool. Outflare pays for none of it.

panels.title: AI tokens by provider
panels.description: Tokens per minute, by provider and kind.

panels.title: AI limits warned and reached
panels.description: Workspaces told their AI spend reached 80% (level 80) or all (level 100) of a limit, per hour.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries by outcome
panels.description: Deliveries connectors (such as Geonode) sent to /v1/hooks per minute. Normal is mostly accepted with a few duplicates; bad_signature or not_found in bulk means a wrong secret, an old address, or someone probing.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries by connector
panels.description: Deliveries per minute by connector. A connector that drops to zero while it usually sends may have lost its subscription.

panels.title: Webhook events finished, by result
panels.description: Events workers finished per minute: handled, ignored (logged, nothing uses it yet), failed (gave up) and retry. Normal is no failed.

panels.title: Time from arrival to handled (p95)
panels.description: How long an event waits from arriving to a worker finishing it, by connector. Normal is a few seconds; minutes means workers are behind (see the Jobs row, kind hooks.handle).

panels.title: Domain Connect lookups by outcome
panels.description: Lookups per minute when a DNS card opens: available means the person can approve the records at their DNS provider. no_provider, not_onboarded and conflict (a DKIM key, DMARC policy or MX already there, which the provider would keep beside the new one) are normal: the card falls back to a Cloudflare token. lookup_failed should stay near zero.

panels.title: Domain Connect lookup time (p95)
panels.description: How long a lookup takes, DNS and the provider's API included. Usually well under a second; cached answers are instant.

panels.title: Queries by outcome
panels.description: Queries run per minute, by outcome: invalid is SQL the database refused, timeout ran over 15 seconds, unavailable means the query role couldn't be set up. type tables failed counts brand queries that ran without their record type tables; normal is none.

panels.title: Query time
panels.description: How long queries take, at the median and the 95th percentile. Each runs on its own connection, at most 8 at once per server.

panels.title: Usage limits warned and reached
panels.description: Workspaces warned that a paid connection (SEO data, lead data, email verification, page reads) used 80% of a daily or monthly usage limit, or reached it, per hour. Normal: a few a day; a burst means a feature is using far more than usual.

panels.title: Calls stopped at a usage limit
panels.description: Paid connector calls Outflare did not make because the connection reached its limit, per hour, by connector. Normal: zero or a trickle; a steady stream means a feature keeps retrying into a limit and should back off.

panels.title: Items embedded
panels.description: Records, replies, meetings and deals turned into vectors per minute, with the workspace's own AI key. Bursts when a workspace first connects an AI model, then a trickle as things change.

panels.title: Embedding jobs by outcome
panels.description: Embedding jobs per minute: failed means a workspace's provider refused or failed (a bad key, its AI limit reached), and the job tries again on the next tick. A few are normal; a steady stream is not.

panels.title: pgvector and workspaces
panels.description: available is 1 when the database has pgvector; workspaces is how many have meaning-based search on with an AI model that makes embeddings. Without pgvector, search by words works and meaning-based search stays off.

panels.title: Network lookups by outcome
panels.description: Data network lookups per minute from the email finder. answered and unknown are normal; refused_allowance means workspaces that haven't joined used their monthly lookups; refused_limit is one domain's daily limit (a spike can mean someone guessing names at one company); error means the network failed and the finder carried on without it.

panels.title: Addresses shared
panels.description: Addresses joined workspaces shared per minute, by outcome. Sends are shared once they are 7 days old, from the hourly sharing jobs, so this comes in bursts.

panels.title: Members and withdrawals
panels.description: members is how many workspaces have joined; withdrawals_pending is how many left and still have shared data to remove. Withdrawals normally finish within an hour of leaving.

panels.title: Overdue withdrawals and sharing lag
panels.description: overdue is how far past its 30-day promise the latest withdrawal is, and should always be 0. lag is how far behind the furthest-behind member's sharing is, beyond the 7 days a send waits; under an hour or two is normal.

panels.title: Smart list freshness
panels.description: How long since the least recently refreshed smart list was brought up to date. Lists refresh every 15 minutes, so normal is under 20 minutes; failing is lists whose last refresh failed.

panels.title: Smart list refreshes
panels.description: Refreshes per minute by outcome, and how long one takes at the 95th percentile. A refresh is one statement over a workspace's people, stopped after two minutes.

panels.title: Rule outcomes
panels.description: Rules evaluated per minute, by trigger kind and outcome: fired, or why not (no_match is normal; duplicate means a replay was caught; late and before_live are backfills that set nothing off). Absence clocks show as started and stopped.

panels.title: Rule jobs
panels.description: Rule jobs per minute by kind and outcome, and how long the slowest wait for a worker (p95). Normal is a few seconds' wait and no dead jobs.

panels.title: Absence timers
panels.description: Absence timers of active rules that ran out and wait to be handled, and how long the oldest has waited. They are handled every minute, so normal is near 0 and under two minutes.

panels.title: Active rules
panels.description: Active rules in every workspace, by trigger kind.

panels.title: Exclusions (people journeys, broadcasts and sequences leave out)
People left out by exclusions
panels.description: People an exclusion (lists and tags a journey, broadcast or sequence names) left out, per minute: journey (refused entry), broadcast (skipped), sequence (not enrolled). Normal: steady and small next to entries and sends. A sudden jump usually means a big list or a common tag was added to an exclusion; a drop to zero after a change may mean a list was emptied.

panels.title: Conversions sent back, by outcome
panels.description: Conversions per minute sent to ad platforms, by platform and outcome. Mostly sent is normal; skipped means no consent or nothing to match on, failed means the platform refused them.

panels.title: Oldest conversion waiting
panels.description: How long the oldest queued conversion has waited. Normal is under five minutes: the sender runs every two.

panels.title: Campaign changes, by how they ended
panels.description: Changes Outflare made to campaigns on ad platforms per hour (pausing, resuming, setting a daily budget), by platform and outcome. Normal is applied, with the odd unverified when a platform shows the old value for a moment; failed means the platform refused a change (its reason is on the change), and error a database failure.

panels.title: Campaign changes, by kind
panels.description: The same changes by kind: pause, resume or budget. A burst of pauses is usually a brand's kill switch.

panels.title: Flag requests, by surface and outcome
panels.description: Requests per minute to decide a visitor's flags: site is the website script (one per page view on sites that use flags), api is servers. Mostly ok is normal; refused is a bad key, origin or body, error is a failure to read flags.

panels.title: Flag request time (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile time to decide a visitor's flags. Normal is a few milliseconds, since flags are kept in memory; it adds to the time before a page shows its variant.

panels.title: Flags read from memory
panels.description: Share of flag lookups answered from memory rather than Postgres. Each workspace's flags are read at most every 10 seconds per process, so on a busy site this is close to 100%.

panels.title: A/B test results time (p95)
panels.description: 95th percentile time to count an A/B test's results from product events, every goal included (opening a running test's results, or ending it). Normal is under a second for most sites; it grows with a site's traffic, since each look scans the test's events.

panels.title: A/B test results counted, by outcome
panels.description: How often A/B test results are counted (ok) or fail (error, usually the 30-second limit on a big site or the database). Normal is a few a minute when people are looking, and no errors.

panels.title: Consent banner requests, by endpoint and outcome
panels.description: Requests per minute from websites' consent banners: config is the script asking for the banner's settings (on a visitor's first page, then every few minutes), choice is a visitor's choice being kept. Mostly ok is normal; refused is a bad key, origin or body, error is a failure to read or write Postgres.

panels.title: Consent banner request time (p95)
panels.description: How long the consent endpoints take at the 95th percentile. Normal is well under 100 ms; the banner waits for config on a visitor's first page.

panels.title: Consent choices, by action and region
panels.description: Visitors' choices kept per minute: accept_all, reject_all, custom (per category), opt_out (US 'Do not sell or share'), gpc and api (the site's own code). A sudden drop to zero while page views go on means the banner stopped showing or sending.

panels.title: Cookie scans, by outcome
panels.description: Scans of websites for their cookie policy, per hour: ok read at least one page; failed read none (the site was down or blocked OutflareBot). Sites with the consent banner on are scanned weekly, so a few an hour is normal.

panels.title: Cookie reports from browsers, by outcome
panels.description: Reports per minute of a site's cookie and script names from visitors' browsers (at most one a day per browser). Mostly ok is normal; refused is a bad key or origin, error a failure to write to Postgres.

panels.title: Cookies and scripts new to a site
panels.description: Things found on a site for the first time, per hour: known ones go straight into its cookie policy, unknown ones wait for a person to classify them. A steady stream of unknown ones means the vendor catalogue is missing something common.

panels.title: Review page reads by outcome
panels.description: Reads of brands' review pages through each workspace's own page reader, by platform and outcome. Normal: mostly success. A failed read is retried in a browser at once, then the same day after 15 minutes, 1 and 2 hours, then every 4 hours. blocked: the site showed a bot check; page_not_found: a wrong address; not_a_review_page: the site answered but the parser found nothing (it may have changed its page); save_failed: a bug; connector_error: the page reader failed.

panels.title: New reviews kept
panels.description: Reviews kept for the first time, by platform. A page's first read brings its history, so spikes after a page is added are normal.

panels.title: Review pages being read
panels.description: Active review pages by platform, how many failed their last read, and how many wait for the workspace to connect a page reader (no_reader). Normal: few failing.

panels.title: Longest since a review page was tried
panels.description: Time since a read of the least recently tried active page ended, read or failed, by platform; pages with no page reader connected are left out. Pages are read once a day and failures are tried again the same day, so normal is under 25 hours.

panels.title: Pricing page reads by outcome
panels.description: Weekly reads of the brand's and its competitors' pricing pages through each workspace's own page reader. Normal: mostly success, a few a day. blocked: a bot check; no_prices_found: the page answered but the price finder found no price (a wrong address, or a layout it misses); page_not_found: a wrong address; save_failed: a bug; connector_error: the page reader failed.

panels.title: Oldest pricing page read
panels.description: Time since a read of the least recently tried pricing page ended. Normal: under a week (pages are read weekly, failures retried the next day). Over nine days alerts: the scheduler or the pricing.read jobs are stuck.

panels.title: Review pages stuck failing
panels.description: Active review pages whose last 3 or more reads failed, same-day retries in a browser included, by platform and error code. Normal: none. blocked means the site shows a bot check even in a browser, not_a_review_page that the site changed its page, save_failed a bug; page_not_found and connector_* are the workspace's to fix and show on its Reviews page.

panels.title: Social account reads by outcome
panels.description: Reads of social accounts' followers (X and LinkedIn connections, and public profiles through each workspace's own page reader), by channel and outcome. Normal: mostly success. A failed read is tried again the same day after 15 minutes, 1 and 2 hours, then every 4 hours. blocked: a bot check; no_follower_count: the page showed no count (private, suspended, or the site changed); page_not_found or invalid_address: a wrong link; save_failed: a bug; connector_error: the connection failed.

panels.title: Social accounts stuck failing
panels.description: Active social accounts whose last 3 or more reads failed, same-day retries included, by channel and error code. Normal: none. blocked, no_follower_count and save_failed are Outflare's to fix (they alert); the others are the workspace's and show on its Social page.

panels.title: Scheduled syncs (analytics, Search Console, ads, SEO)
Sync runs by outcome
panels.description: Scheduled sync runs of connections, by module and outcome. Normal: mostly success. A failed run is tried again soon (15 minutes, then 1, 2 and every 4 hours) instead of after its whole interval. internal: Outflare's own bug; connector_auth or connector_quota: the workspace's key or plan; connector_unavailable: the provider failed; budget_reached: an SEO budget doing its job.

panels.title: Syncs stuck failing
panels.description: Syncs of connected connections whose last 3 or more runs failed, retries included, by module and error code. Normal: none, or a few connector_auth (a workspace's expired key). internal, connector_unavailable and unknown alert.

panels.title: Ad sets, ads and keywords synced
panels.description: Days of numbers the ad sync stores below campaigns: ad groups (Meta ad sets, Google ad groups) and ads, and Google keywords and search terms. Normal: a burst every six hours per connected account, larger the first time an account syncs (90 days). Flat at zero while ads sync runs succeed means the platforms list nothing below campaigns, or their reports came back empty.

panels.title: Posts by outcome
panels.description: Posts the publish job tried per hour, by channel and outcome. Normal is all published; failed means the channel refused a post or did not answer (each one is listed with its reason under Social); retried is a rate limit before anything was posted.

panels.title: Most overdue approved post
panels.description: How long past its time the most overdue approved post is, by channel. Posts go out within a minute or two of their time, so normal is near zero.

panels.title: Approved posts waiting
panels.description: Approved posts not out yet, by channel and state: later is scheduled ahead (normal), due is waiting for the publish job and should stay near zero.

panels.title: Actions sent to Engain
panels.description: Reddit campaign actions sent to Engain per hour, by kind and outcome. Normal is all submitted; failed means Engain refused it, unknown that it did not answer so the action may or may not exist (each one is listed with its reason under Reddit).

panels.title: Checks of sent actions
panels.description: Checks of sent actions per hour on Engain and on Reddit as a logged-out visitor sees them, by outcome. Normal is mostly ok with reddit_read true; reddit_error means Reddit turned the reader away (connect Geonode), engain_error that Engain did not answer.

panels.title: Link building (who links to a page, on workspaces' own SEO connections)
Link reads by reason and outcome
panels.description: Reads of who links to a page or domain, per hour: requested by people, agents and playbooks, or the weekly read of competitors' dead pages (dead_page). Normal: mostly success, in a burst after the weekly SEO snapshot. budget_reached means a connection's budget or the workspace's weekly share ran out; provider_error or connector_auth rising means Ahrefs or DataForSEO is failing or a key was revoked.

panels.title: Link prospect page checks by status
panels.description: OutflareBot's checks of link prospects' pages, per hour, by what it found. Normal: mostly up, some gone, blocked or unreachable (other people's sites). failed rising means checks are breaking: look for link_prospect.check_failed in the log.

panels.title: Internet Archive lookups by outcome
panels.description: Lookups of broken links in the Internet Archive, per hour. Normal: found and none; error rising means archive.org is slow or down, and checks go on without snapshots.

panels.title: Link pitch openers written, by outcome
panels.description: Openers the workspaces' own AI wrote for link pitches, per hour. Normal: mostly written; no_ai and ai_unavailable are workspaces without AI connected or over their limit. ai_failed rising means the model's answers broke: check link_pitches.write jobs.

panels.title: Link pitch replies read, by kind
panels.description: Replies to link pitches the workspaces' AI read, per hour, by what they say. Normal: a mix of other, declined and agreed, with few wants_payment. ai_failed rising means reading broke: check link_pitches.read_reply jobs.

panels.title: Agreed and live link checks, by outcome
panels.description: Checks of links sites agreed to add, and of live ones, per hour. Normal: mostly not_yet and still_live, some live; removed is a site taking a link down. unreachable high for hours means OutflareBot can't reach pages: check link_live.schedule_failed in the log.

panels.title: Web searches, by outcome
panels.description: Searches on workspaces' own DataForSEO or Geonode (search-results, used by link building playbooks), per hour. Normal: mostly done, some budget_reached. connector_unavailable or connector_invalid rising means the provider's search API is failing or changed: check web_search.done and api.called for readSearchResults by error code.

panels.title: Link pitches sent without approval, by outcome
panels.description: Pitches through sequences that skip approval, per hour: sent, or why they wait. Normal: mostly sent, with some unsure or spammy_site waiting for a person. daily_cap means a sequence hit its daily limit; those go out on later days (alert OutflareLinkPitchesHeldByCap if they pile up).

panels.title: News watch (saved news searches, on workspaces' own web search connections)
News search runs by outcome
panels.description: Runs of saved news searches through each workspace's own web search connection, by purpose and outcome. Normal: mostly success; connector_needed means a workspace has searches but no web search connection, usage_limit_reached that its connection hit a limit, connector_error that the provider failed.

panels.title: News searches and what they find
panels.description: Active news searches by state (failing: the last run failed), and the articles and coverage items runs keep for the first time per hour. Normal: few failing searches; finds rise and fall with the news.

panels.title: Most overdue news search
panels.description: How long past its time the most overdue active news search is. Searches are queued every minute, so this stays near 0; it climbing means the scheduler or the news.run jobs are stuck.

panels.title: News article reads
panels.description: OutflareBot's reads of new news articles for their byline, by status, and how many found a new journalist. Normal: mostly up; blocked and opted_out are sites saying no, unreachable and failed are worth a look when they climb.

panels.title: Story ideas, release drafts, pitches and replies
panels.description: The workspace's own AI suggesting story ideas, drafting releases, writing pitch openers and reading journalists' replies, by kind (ideas, draft, pitch, reply) and outcome. Normal: mostly success; ai_model_needed and ai_budget_reached are workspaces to set up, ai_failed and connector_auth climbing are worth a look.

panels.title: Quote approval emails and experts' decisions
panels.description: Emails asking PR experts to approve a quote, as their outreach sequences finished them (sent, blocked by the send policy, failed, bounced), and the experts' decisions through their links. Normal: mostly sent; blocked is a suppressed or unverified address; failed or bounced climbing means the sequences' mailboxes can't deliver.

panels.title: Partner conversions, by outcome
panels.description: Sign-ups, sales, refunds and custom conversions per minute reported by workspaces' backends (api) and postback URLs, by type and outcome. not_credited is normal (most customers weren't referred); rejected is bad input from the sender; error is ours.

panels.title: Partner link clicks, by outcome
panels.description: Clicks per minute on partners' short links (/r/<code>). tracked is normal; inactive is a paused program or partner (the visitor still lands); not_found is an unknown code; error means the click wasn't stored.

panels.title: Reward ledger changes
panels.description: Ledger entries per minute by kind and event: created by conversions, approved when their hold ends, reversed by refunds, paid through payouts.

panels.title: Oldest reward past its hold
panels.description: How long the oldest reward that should approve on its own has waited past its hold. Normal is under two minutes: the approver runs every minute.

panels.title: Partner imports from Tolt, by outcome
panels.description: Imports of partner programs from another platform (Tolt) that finished in the last hour, by connector and outcome. Imports are rare: a few runs around a workspace's switch-over day. failed means the platform refused the key, the program wasn't found or it kept failing; the import's own page says why.

panels.title: Objects partner imports read, by kind and result
panels.description: What imports did with each object they read, per minute: created here, updated (a status brought over), unchanged (here already, normal on a second run) or skipped (listed on the import as an issue). A lot of skipped means the platform's data doesn't fit; look at the import's issues.

panels.title: Postbacks to partners' trackers, by outcome
panels.description: Calls to affiliates' own trackers per hour. sent is normal; retried and unreachable are a tracker that is down (theirs) or this server unable to reach outside addresses; rejected is a tracker that refused the URL (the partner's template).

panels.title: Meeting events recorded, by status
panels.description: Meeting events per minute recorded on people's timelines (meeting.booked, held, no_show, canceled), from calendars, CRMs, the app and the API. It follows how many meetings are booked and change; a backfill after an upgrade shows as one burst.

panels.title: Meetings waiting for their event
panels.description: Meetings tied to a person whose latest status isn't on their timeline yet. Normal is near zero, drained every minute; a backlog that stays means the meeting events loop is failing (meeting_events.run_failed in the log).

panels.title: Redirect link clicks, by outcome
panels.description: Clicks per minute on campaign redirect links (/l/{code}): counted is a person, bot a link scanner or preview, unknown a code that isn't a link (old or mistyped), error a click that couldn't be stored (the person was still sent on). Mostly counted is normal; any steady error means clicks are being lost, usually the database.

panels.title: Redirect clicks reaching the site, by outcome
panels.description: Page views per minute that carried a redirect click's key (ofclk), so the site's script could tie the visit to the click: claimed means the visit took the click, unmatched a reload of the same landing page or a key from another workspace. Claimed should follow counted redirect clicks for sites that run the script; claimed near zero while clicks are counted means site.js isn't reading ofclk (an old saved copy, or the landing pages don't load the script).

panels.title: Redirect clicks written, by outcome
panels.description: Redirect clicks per minute by what happened when their batch was written a moment after the redirect: written is normal and follows clicks; refused_quota is a workspace over its click quota (the people were still sent on); link_gone is rare; failed means the batch couldn't be written and waits for the next flush; dropped_full means too many waited and new clicks were lost.

panels.title: Redirect clicks waiting, and batch write time
panels.description: Clicks waiting in each process to be written (a few hundred at most is normal; it grows while the database can't take them, and new clicks are dropped past 100,000), and the 95th percentile time to write a batch of up to 1,000 (normal is well under 100 ms).

panels.title: Ad tracking health (paid clicks arriving on sites)
Paid ad landings, by how they were tracked
panels.description: Landing pages per minute from paid ads (a paid utm_medium), by outcome: click_id is the network's own click id (best), ad_ids only the tracking template's ad ids, none neither, which means the ad has no tracking template and can be credited only by its UTM tags. Mostly click_id is normal; a network that is mostly none has ads without the template (Paid ads → Tracking templates).

panels.title: Unfilled tracking template macros, by network
panels.description: Template values per minute that arrived as the macro itself ({{ad.id}}, __CID__) because the network didn't fill it in. Zero is normal. A steady line for one network means its macro in the template is wrong: check engine/internal/adtrack against that network's docs.

panels.title: Questions asked of knowledge, by outcome
panels.description: Questions per minute from the Ask box, agents and MCP: answered (the knowledge covers it), unanswered (a gap someone could write), no_ai (no AI model connected or the AI limit reached; passages only) and error. Normal is mostly answered; a rising share of error means the AI providers are failing (knowledge.answer_failed in the log).

panels.title: Time to answer from knowledge
panels.description: How long a question takes: finding the passages and the AI model writing the answer, on the workspace's own key. Normal is a few seconds at the 95th percentile; slower means the AI provider is slow.

panels.title: Journey webhooks, Slack, sequencers and AI steps
Journey calls
panels.description: Calls made by journeys' webhook, Slack, push_to_sequencer and AI steps, per minute, by kind and outcome. Normal: mostly done; skipped is a call with nothing to do (a person already in the campaign). retried is a try that will be tried again (the receiver answered 5xx or 429, or didn't answer); failed is a call that gave up or was refused (4xx, or Slack refused the channel). A rise in failed for one kind usually means a receiver changed or a key expired: the run's history says which step.

panels.title: Journey call time (p95)
panels.description: How long one try of a journey call takes at the 95th percentile, by kind. Normal: under a second. Calls give up after 20 seconds; time near that means a receiver is slow or not answering.

panels.title: People added to sequencer campaigns
panels.description: People journeys' push_to_sequencer steps added to Smartlead, Instantly and EmailBison campaigns, per minute, by connector and outcome. Normal: mostly added, some already_in (a person who was already there) and refused (the sequencer left them out: in another campaign, unsubscribed or blocked there). error is the sequencer failing or refusing the workspace's key; a run's history says which journey.

panels.title: People created or updated in CRMs
panels.description: People journeys' push_to_crm steps created or updated in the workspace's CRM (HubSpot), per minute, by connector and outcome. Normal: created and updated. error is the CRM failing, refusing the workspace's key, or not having a property a step names; the run's history says which journey.

panels.title: People added to or removed from ad audiences
panels.description: People journeys' sync_audience steps added to or removed from customer list audiences on the workspace's ad accounts (Meta, Google Ads), per minute, by connector and outcome. Normal: added and removed, with some skipped (no ad consent, or no email or phone). error is the platform failing or refusing the workspace's key, or an audience it won't fill (Meta's Custom Audience terms not accepted); the run's history says which journey.

panels.title: Inbound email (workspaces' forwarded mail: support, AI receipts)
Inbound messages delivered, by outcome
panels.description: Messages the operator's edge delivered per hour: accepted, duplicate (the same Message-ID again), unknown_address (refused: no such address), bad_signature, too_large or error. Mostly accepted is normal, with some unknown_address from old or mistyped addresses; any bad_signature means the edge and the engine disagree on the inbound secret, and any error is the database.

panels.title: Inbound messages processed, by purpose and status
panels.description: What became of delivered messages per hour: processed (handled, or a Gmail forwarding confirmation kept), ignored (nothing for its purpose), rejected (refused, usually forwarded by an address nobody linked) or failed (Outflare's error, retried). Failed should be zero; rejected that grows fast means people forward from addresses they haven't linked.

panels.title: Inbound mail received
panels.description: Size of the accepted messages per hour, and raw messages deleted after 30 days (their details stay). Received grows with forwarding; the database holds up to 30 days of it.

panels.title: Exchange rate age and receipts converted
panels.description: How old the newest exchange rate is (the European Central Bank publishes one each working day, so up to 3 days at a weekend is normal), and receipts in other currencies given their dollar amount per hour once a rate arrived. Only servers with inbound email fetch rates.

panels.title: Support messages, by kind and outcome
panels.description: Messages per minute in the support inbox: in (customers writing to a support mailbox, stored by the mailbox sync), out (replies the team queued) and note, by outcome. Normal follows the working day; in at zero for hours while customers usually write means the support mailboxes stopped syncing (see the mailbox sync panels and sync_error on the mailboxes).

panels.title: Support replies sent, by outcome
panels.description: Replies the support.send job finished per minute: sent, failed (the address is blocked, the mailbox is gone or paused, or its server refused after every retry) and retry (a connection error, tried again). Normal is nearly all sent.

panels.title: Time to send a support reply
panels.description: How long one reply takes to go out through its mailbox's SMTP server. Normal is a second or two at the 95th percentile; slower means the mail servers are slow to accept.

panels.title: Support replies waiting to send
panels.description: Replies queued and not yet picked up by a worker, and how long the oldest has waited. Normal is zero and a few seconds; a growing wait means the workers are behind (see the job queue row).

panels.title: Support SLA targets missed, by target
panels.description: Replies (reply) and resolutions (resolve) that ran past the time a workspace's SLA promised, per hour, across workspaces. These are the teams' misses, not Outflare faults; normal is whatever your customers' teams run at, and a sudden jump with no change in traffic points at the SLA check.

panels.title: Support conversations past their SLA
panels.description: Conversations not closed that are past an SLA target right now, by target, across workspaces. Moves with how busy support teams are.

panels.title: Support SLA checks, by outcome
panels.description: Runs of the check that marks missed SLA targets, per minute. Normal is about one success a minute per worker process and no errors.

panels.title: Time for one support SLA check
panels.description: 95th percentile of one SLA check. Normal is well under a second; it grows with the number of conversations due at once.

panels.title: Journey runs waiting
panels.description: Runs on a wait_until step, waiting for an event, for conditions to come true, or for their timeout. It grows with journeys that wait days; a sudden jump usually means a new journey with a long wait went live.

panels.title: Most overdue journey run
panels.description: How long past its time the most overdue run of an active journey is. Normal: under a minute. Higher means journey jobs aren't running or are far behind: check the job queue panels.

panels.title: Journey entries turned away
panels.description: People a journey's trigger would have started but its entry limit (limit) or re-entry wait (reentry) turned away, per minute. Expected when a busy trigger meets a low limit; a steady high rate may mean the limit is too low.

panels.title: Help centre requests, by page and outcome
panels.description: Requests per minute to public help centres (/h/ and their own domains): home, collection, article, search, feedback, markdown, sitemap and llms pages, by outcome. Normal is almost all ok, some not_found (old links, closed help centres); limited is one network reading too fast; any steady error or count_failed means the database is struggling.

panels.title: Time to build a help centre page
panels.description: How long the server takes to build a help centre page, its database reads included. Normal is well under 100 ms; over a second at the 95th percentile means a very large help centre or a slow database.

panels.title: Playbook automations (playbooks that run by themselves)
Playbook automation runs, by kind and outcome
panels.description: Runs per hour that playbook automations started (started), held for a person (held: a spend limit, a connection or the AI model missing, the approver gone), failed and will retry in 15 minutes (failed), or left for tomorrow by the daily cap (capped). Mostly started, with the odd held, is normal; steady failed means runs can't be created, usually the database: check playbook_automation.run_failed in the engine log.

panels.title: Most overdue playbook automation
panels.description: How long the most overdue active automation has waited past its run time, at the last pass (every minute). Under two minutes is normal. A climbing line means the automation loop is stuck or slow: check playbook_automation.runner_failed in the engine log.

panels.title: Product events sent to brands (event inbox)
Product events received and processed, by outcome
panels.description: Events per minute sent to POST /v1/brands/{brand}/events (received) and what the events.process job made of them: accepted, duplicate (a messageId the brand already had), rejected (something to fix, kept 90 days) or held (a name the catalog hasn't approved). Normal is processed keeping up with received and mostly accepted; a jump in rejected usually means one sender changed what it sends.

panels.title: Rejected product events, by code
panels.description: Events per minute the job rejected, by code (missing_id, invalid_timestamp, property_type, other_brand, internal and the rest). Normal is near zero; a steady code says what senders get wrong, and any internal means events failed five times for a database reason (see the logs for customer_events.process_failed).

panels.title: Product events waiting, and the oldest one's wait
panels.description: Events saved but not processed yet, and how long the oldest has waited. Normal is a few events for a few seconds; a wait over five minutes means the job queue is behind or events.process keeps failing (the Job queue row shows which).

panels.title: Time to process one product event
panels.description: How long the job takes per event, matching the person and writing the event. Normal is a few milliseconds; over a second at the 95th percentile means heavy identity matching (many merges) or a slow database.

panels.title: Event inbox retention sweep
panels.description: Rows deleted per minute at the end of their retention (30 days accepted, 90 rejected or held), and how far past its retention the oldest row still waiting is. Normal is deletions in bursts every ten minutes and an overdue time under an hour; a growing overdue time means the sweep is failing (customer_events.purge_failed in the logs).

panels.title: Marketing email guardrails (frequency cap, quiet hours)
Marketing emails capped or held
panels.description: Marketing emails from journeys and broadcasts that a workspace's guardrails stopped (frequency_cap: the person already got their limit, so it isn't sent) or held (quiet_hours: sent when the person's quiet hours end), per minute. Normal: a small share of what journeys and broadcasts send. A sudden rise in frequency_cap usually means a workspace started a broadcast or journey that overlaps another; each capped send is email.capped on the person's timeline.

panels.title: Desktop reports and readings
panels.description: Reports from linked computers per hour by outcome, and usage windows read per hour by provider and source. Mostly ok reports is normal; error means Outflare failed to store one (the database), invalid an app sending something the API refuses (an old or broken version).

panels.title: Linked computers and tools they couldn't read
panels.description: Computers reporting in the last hour and silent ones (off, asleep or the app quit: normal at night), and tools the apps couldn't read per hour by provider and code. not_signed_in is the person's to fix; a jump in bad_response or forbidden for one provider usually means it changed its endpoint: switch that source off (ai_desktop_sources_off) until the app is fixed.

panels.title: Privacy exports built, by outcome
panels.description: Privacy exports per hour the privacy_export.build job finished: ready, too_large (over 100 MB uncompressed), record_gone (the record went before the build), internal (the build kept failing; privacy_export.build_failed in the logs) or error (an attempt that will be retried), and files deleted after their 7 days (expired). Normal is a few, almost all ready; any internal is worth a look.

panels.title: Privacy export build time and size
panels.description: How long one privacy export takes to build (p50, p95) and how big the uncompressed file is (p95, right axis in bytes). Normal is under a few seconds and under a few MB; minutes or sizes near 100 MB mean a record with a very long history, which fails with too_large past the limit.

panels.title: Customer data deleted into the recovery window, by kind
panels.description: Records, field values, identities, links and product events deleted per hour into Recently deleted, where they can be restored for 7 days. Normal is a handful; a burst means someone (or an agent) is deleting in bulk, which the audit log (record.soft_deleted, customer_event.deleted and the rest) says.

panels.title: Deletions restored, by kind and outcome
panels.description: Deletions restored per hour from Recently deleted. partly_restored and not_restored mean some rows couldn't come back (a unique value taken since, the other end erased, or a field set again); the answer and the deletion's not_restored list say which. Normal is mostly restored.

panels.title: Recovery window purge
panels.description: Deletions purged per hour once their 7 days are over (a deleted record is erased then), and how far past its 7 days the oldest deletion still waiting is. Normal is purges in rounds every ten minutes and an overdue time under an hour; a growing overdue time means the purge is failing (deletion.purge_failed in the logs) and deleted data is kept longer than promised.

panels.title: Review dispatch results
panels.description: Normal dispatch jobs succeed; retried or dead jobs need attention in the job log.

panels.title: Review dispatch delay
panels.description: Due campaign batches should be picked up promptly; scheduled future campaigns are excluded.

panels.title: Review dispatch duration
panels.description: 95th percentile processing time for a batch of up to 50 review invitations. Rising time can indicate slow eligibility queries.

panels.title: Coverage checks
panels.description: Observed availability; blocked and unreachable reads need investigation when sustained.

panels.title: Coverage job backlog
panels.description: Checks normally begin within a few minutes. A rising age means workers need attention.

panels.title: Coverage worker failures
panels.description: Retries can occur on transient database errors; dead jobs need investigation.

panels.title: Presence discovery
panels.description: Pages discovery added to brands' review lists, by source, and web search runs by outcome. Finds come in bursts once a day; sustained connector errors need a look at the search results connectors.

panels.title: Where competitors appear
panels.description: Competitor presence scans by source and outcome, new pages found where a competitor appears, by whether they look paid for, and opportunities suggested and won. Scans run weekly or monthly per competitor; connector_needed is normal until a workspace connects a search results or SEO connection, while sustained connector or provider errors need a look. Also the daily look for new competitors: looks that worked (ok) or failed (error) and the competitors suggested, by source; normally one look a site a day and a few suggestions.

panels.title: Coverage accuracy review results
panels.description: Reviewed is a completed assessment. Missing Knowledge or model connections need workspace configuration; review failures need investigation.

panels.title: Merges undone and batch undos
panels.description: Merges undone (unmerges) and import or ingest batches undone per hour, by mode and outcome. Normal is rare and small; refused unmerges are merges too old to undo or with a later merge to undo first. failed batch undos changed nothing (job.dead for batches.undo in the log) and fire OutflareBatchUndoFailing.

panels.title: Rows reverted by undos, and batch undo time
panels.description: Rows moved back, removed or put back per hour by unmerges and batch undos, and the 95th percentile time to undo one batch. Normal is a few rows and well under a minute; a batch of tens of thousands takes longer and runs in a job.

panels.title: Partner task checks
panels.description: Ownership, audience reach and submitted link checks. Successful jobs can leave evidence for human review; retries or dead jobs need investigation.

panels.title: Partner task check backlog
panels.description: Seconds the oldest due check has waited. Future review holds are not due and should not appear here. Normally near zero.

panels.title: Saved queries run and CSV downloads
panels.description: Saved queries run from Query Studio or run_saved_query, and query results downloaded as CSV, per hour, by outcome. They run through the same query path as above, so their failures show there too. Normal: follows how much people use Query Studio; many invalid saved runs mean saved SQL broke, often after a field or type was archived.

panels.title: Rows downloaded as CSV
panels.description: Rows written to CSV downloads of query results per hour (each download holds at most 10,000). Every download is a query.exported entry in the workspace's activity log. Normal: small and bursty; a steady high level means something downloads customer data in bulk on a schedule.

panels.title: Older mailbox sign-ins moved into connections
panels.description: Mailbox sign-ins from before they were Gmail and Outlook connections, moved at start-up, per hour, by kind (admin: a service account or Entra app; sign_in: one mailbox's own sign-in) and outcome. Normal: a burst of moved and linked on the first start of this version, then nothing. failed is a row that could not be read or saved; it is tried again at every start, and mailbox.sign_in_move_failed in the logs names its workspace.

panels.title: Knowledge review queue (suggested answers and conflicts)
Knowledge review queue, by outcome
panels.description: What happened to suggestions for the knowledge review queue per hour: created (an answer from a teammate's support reply, an agent, the website or Slack, or a conflict noticed while answering), approved or rejected by a person, and for support replies not_reusable (only about one customer), no_ai (the workspace has no AI model) or error. Normal is mostly created, approved and not_reusable; error should stay near zero.

panels.title: Knowledge suggestions, by source
panels.description: Suggestions created per hour by where they came from: support_reply, website, slack, agent, person, answer (a conflict). Moves with how much support and AI answering workspaces do.

panels.title: Website chat (chat widgets on businesses' sites)
Website chat requests, by route
panels.description: Requests from chat widgets on businesses' websites per minute: loader and frame (opening the chat), session, poll (checking for replies every few seconds while open), send and articles. Normal is mostly poll, and grows with how many visitors have a chat open.

panels.title: Website chat requests refused or failing, by outcome
panels.description: Chat requests that didn't succeed per minute: limited (rate limits per network and visitor), not_found (a removed or switched-off widget still on a site), bad_token, invalid and error. Normal is a little not_found and limited; error should stay at zero.

panels.title: Personal Gmail capture jobs
panels.description: Read-only CRM Google capture jobs, grouped by outcome. Eligible connected users poll roughly every five minutes; zero jobs is normal with no connected users. Retries or dead jobs need investigation. No mailbox or user labels are emitted.

panels.title: Email privacy checks
panels.description: Emails the AI privacy check read before team email sharing shows them to colleagues, per second by outcome: work (shared), private (kept to its owner), failed, no_ai (no AI model connected) or budget (the AI limit was reached). Zero is normal when no brand has team sharing on. A steady failed, no_ai or budget line means colleagues aren't seeing new work email.

panels.title: Lifecycle checks by outcome
panels.description: Lifecycle checks per minute, by level (company, person; any before a level is known) and outcome. moved is someone changing stage; no_move is usual. before_live (events from before a brand turned stages on), not_approved (held event names) and late are expected in small numbers; a steady rise in duplicate means events are being replayed.

panels.title: Lifecycle jobs
panels.description: lifecycle.event jobs per minute by outcome, and how long they waited in the queue (p95). Normal: no dead jobs and a wait of seconds.

panels.title: Inactivity checks due
panels.description: Inactivity checks (at risk, churned for no usage) that fell due and wait for the sweep, and how long the oldest has waited. Normal is near 0 and under two minutes: the sweep runs every minute, 200 at a time per worker.

panels.title: Inactivity sweep duration
panels.description: How long one inactivity sweep takes (p95). Normal is well under a second; a sweep that takes many seconds is handling a backlog.

panels.title: Agent changes, by what the gate did and why
panels.description: Changes per hour that agent tokens on the action layer made: run by a grant (running), held for a person (held: no grant matched, a grant holds it, a daily limit was reached, or it always needs a person), or refused by a grant. Mostly running and held is normal for agents people trust; a sudden jump in held usually means a grant was revoked or a daily limit is too low.

panels.title: How agent changes ended
panels.description: Per hour: changes that ran (executed), ran and got an error answer (failed), or a person turned down (rejected). Some failed is normal (an agent sending a bad request); a steady rise means an agent keeps trying something the API refuses: look at its actions with status=failed.

panels.title: Held agent changes waiting for a person
panels.description: How many agent changes wait for a person across every workspace, from the database scrape. It rises while agents work and falls as people decide. A line that only climbs means nobody is deciding: the approval inbox is GET .../actions?status=held.

panels.title: Longest wait for a person, and changes stuck running
panels.description: How long the oldest held change has waited (left axis, seconds), and changes claimed to run over 15 minutes ago that never recorded how they ended (normally 0). A stuck change means an engine stopped mid-run: check action result in the engine log.

panels.title: Support assistant runs, by action
panels.description: Customer messages the support assistant looked at per hour: answer and clarify are drafts for a person to send, handoff went to a person, skipped was stopped before the AI (automatic mail, a teammate on it), failed means the AI call broke. Normal follows support volume, with failed near zero.

panels.title: Support assistant time to decide (p95)
panels.description: How long the assistant takes to decide on one message at the 95th percentile, model calls and checks included. Normal is a few seconds to about 20; a chat visitor waits on it.

panels.title: Missing-answer searches, by source and outcome
panels.description: Each time the assistant had no answer, its search of the website and then the picked Slack channels, per hour: found (suggested in Knowledge), none, nothing_to_read, off, no_ai or error. Normal is mostly none and some found; error should stay near zero.

panels.title: Website pages imported into knowledge, by result
panels.description: Pages website imports handled per hour: added as new articles, updated because the page changed, or unchanged. Normal is bursts when someone runs an import, mostly unchanged on later runs.

panels.title: Held Auto email replies, by result
panels.description: What became of Auto email replies that waited their hold, per hour: sent when it ended, stopped by a teammate, cancelled (the team replied, the customer wrote again or it was closed), refused by the send, or left as a draft because Auto was turned off. Normal: mostly sent, a few stopped; refused should stay near zero.

panels.title: Website re-checks and learning from past replies
panels.description: Daily website re-checks the scheduler queued, and runs that learned answers from past support replies, per hour, by outcome. Normal: re-checks spread through the day for each workspace with an imported website; learning runs only when someone starts one, nearly all done.

panels.title: Calls to MCP servers, by operation and outcome
panels.description: Calls per minute Outflare made to MCP servers: connecting, listing tools and calling them. Mostly success is normal; a share of error means a server is down, refused the credentials, or sits on a private address that isn't allowed.

panels.title: MCP call time (p95), by operation
panels.description: How long the slowest 5% of calls to MCP servers took. Tool calls that drive a browser can take tens of seconds; a climb toward two minutes means calls are timing out.

panels.title: Agent runs (Outflare's agent on the action layer)
Agent run turns an hour, by how they ended
panels.description: Turns Outflare's agent took in agent runs (playbooks started on the action layer). Normal: mostly done; failed means the model or the API broke (three in a row pause the run); paused is a run that stopped itself with a reason a person acts on.

panels.title: Agent runs live, and the most overdue turn
panels.description: Runs taking turns (running) or waiting for a person (paused), and how long past its time the most overdue running run's next turn is. Normal: overdue near 0; over 15 minutes means the runner isn't running.

panels.title: Quota refusals
panels.description: Work an extension's quota refused, per hour, by resource: new brands, mailboxes, tracking domains or records answered 402 quota_exceeded, and emails held back to try again in an hour. Normal: none on a self-hosted server (no quota); on a hosted one, a few from workspaces past their plan.

panels.title: Quota checks failing
panels.description: Quota checks where the extension's checker failed, per hour, by resource. The work was allowed anyway. Normal: none; any means the checker (its database or service) is broken and plan limits aren't being applied.

panels.title: Metrics (live totals per company and person)
Metric updates by outcome
panels.description: Events added to live metrics per minute. updated is normal; backfilled (counted by a fill) and too_old (before the window) are expected in small numbers; a steady no_value means a metric's property isn't a number in the events.

panels.title: Metric jobs
panels.description: metric.event and metric.backfill jobs per minute by outcome, and their queue wait (p95). Normal: no dead jobs, waits of seconds.

panels.title: Metric windows waiting
panels.description: Values whose window moved (a new UTC day) and wait for the sweep, how long the oldest has waited, and metrics refilling now. Normal: a burst just after midnight UTC that clears in minutes.

panels.title: Metric fill and sweep duration
panels.description: How long a metric's fill from stored events (p95, by outcome) and one window sweep (p95) take. Fills of large brands can take minutes; sweeps should stay under a few seconds.

panels.title: Bulk edits finished
panels.description: Bulk edits and undos owners ran, by outcome, per hour. Normal: a few done a day, none failed.

panels.title: Records bulk edited
panels.description: Records bulk edits went through per hour: changed, unchanged (already so) and skipped (deleted or merged since). A spike is an owner's large edit.

panels.title: Bulk edits waiting
panels.description: Bulk edits queued or running, and how long the oldest has waited, with p95 run time. Normal: 0, or one for a few minutes while an edit runs.

panels.title: Query endpoint calls
panels.description: Calls to published query endpoints per minute by outcome and error code. Normal: mostly success; some rate_limited or invalid_request is a caller's mistake; error means Outflare failed to answer.

panels.title: Query endpoint time and rows
panels.description: How long calls take (p95, seconds) and rows returned per minute. Normal: well under the 30-second query limit.

panels.title: Publications to CMSs, by how they ended
panels.description: Posts and pages Outflare published to brands' own CMSs per hour (WordPress, Ghost), by connector and outcome. Normal is applied, with the odd unverified when the CMS shows a different status for a moment; failed means the CMS refused it (its reason is on the publication), and error a database failure.

panels.title: Publications to CMSs, by kind
panels.description: The same publications by kind: create (a new post on the CMS) or update (the post the item already is). Normal: a handful a day per brand that publishes.

panels.title: Hand edits expired
panels.description: Hand edits whose time to win ran out, per hour: switched (another source's value took over, as a change in the record's history), kept (no other source had a value; the next one to write replaces it) and error. Normal: a steady trickle 180 days after people's edits; any error is worth a look in the logs (hand_edit.expire_failed).

panels.title: Hand edits waiting for the sweep
panels.description: Expired hand edits the sweep hasn't handed over yet, and how long the oldest has waited. The sweep runs every 5 minutes, so normal is 0 and under 10 minutes; a growing wait means the sweep isn't running or keeps failing.

panels.title: Transactions saved
panels.description: Payments, refunds, chargebacks and credits sent to Outflare per hour, from the API and billing connectors, by outcome. Normal: created, with some duplicate (the same source id again, such as a retry or a sync reading it twice). invalid is a caller's mistake; any error is worth a look in the logs.

panels.title: Transactions without a converted amount
panels.description: Transactions over 2 days old still without an amount in their brand's currency, and p95 time to save one. Normal: 0 unconverted (exchange rates come in daily) and well under a second.

panels.title: Account uses an hour, by outcome
panels.description: Managed sign-ins, verifications and session uses of brands' external accounts, by outcome. Normal is authenticated with the odd verification pending or MFA waiting; credential failures, wrong identities and locked accounts open incidents a person resolves.

panels.title: Open account incidents, by severity
panels.description: Incidents open on brands' external accounts right now, by severity. Normal: a handful of info and warning; critical ones (a credential refused, a wrong identity, a locked account) stop automated use until a person acts.

panels.title: Account takeovers waiting for a person
panels.description: Takeover requests (a managed use met MFA, a CAPTCHA, a passkey or a consent screen) that no person has started yet, and how long the oldest has waited. Normal is zero most of the time; a request that waits hours means the brand's work on that account is stuck.

panels.title: Account takeovers a day, by step
panels.description: Human takeovers of brands' external accounts: requested, started by a person, handed back (with the identity checked), cancelled. Normal is a few a day; many requests with few handbacks means people are not answering them.

panels.title: Browser workers (tasks in a browser on sites with no API)
Browser tasks waiting, running and waiting for a person
panels.description: Browser tasks by state. Queued tasks that stay mean no worker with Chrome is running (OUTFLARE_ROLE=browser) or they are all busy; waiting_person tasks resume when a person hands the account back. Normal is a few in each state that move within minutes.

panels.title: Oldest queued browser task
panels.description: How long the oldest queued browser task has waited for a worker. Normal is under a minute with a browser worker running; it grows without one.

panels.title: Browser task runs a day, by how they ended
panels.description: Runs of browser tasks: done, failed, or waiting_person (MFA, a CAPTCHA, a passkey or a consent screen asked for a person). Normal is mostly done; many failed means sites changed, sign-ins are refused or the worker has no AI or Chrome.

panels.title: Browser task steps an hour, by tool
panels.description: Tool calls browser tasks make: navigate, read_page, click, type, type_content, fill_secret, report_sign_in, need_person, finish. The mix says what the tasks do; fill_secret and need_person are the sign-ins.

panels.title: Saved sign-in sessions a day
panels.description: Saved sessions of brand accounts: restored (a task started signed in), saved (a run that confirmed the account's identity kept its cookies) and cleared (the wrong identity, a locked account, a refused credential, or too old). Normal is mostly restored and saved; many cleared means accounts were signed out or changed hands.

panels.title: Connections and brands (no brand, no data)
Connections and accounts with no brand
panels.description: Brand connections with no brand (connection) and analytics or Search Console sites and ad accounts nobody assigned (account), across every workspace, counted every ten minutes. Their data is stored but shows in no brand until someone assigns it on the Connectors page. Normal: low and falling after people connect something; a count that keeps growing means new sites or accounts arrive faster than anyone assigns them. A flat line with no data means the count is failing (integration.unassigned_count_failed in the log).

panels.title: Suggestions made, by kind
panels.description: Changes Outflare suggested for campaigns per hour, by kind. They come after each ad sync; none for days means no sync ran or no campaign has a target.

panels.title: Verdicts on approved suggestions
panels.description: Approved suggestions judged after their measuring window, by verdict. Mostly not_sure means windows end with too few conversions.

panels.title: Suggestion runs, by outcome
panels.description: Runs of the suggestions job per hour (one per workspace after each ad sync), by outcome. Normal is all success.

panels.title: Insight runs an hour, by kind and how they ended
panels.description: Insight queries people and agents ran (funnel, funnel_people, trend, retention), tiles of shared dashboards (shared), the hourly checks of alerts on a number (alert_check) and dashboards in the digest (digest): success, invalid (a spec the caller can fix), timeout (over 30 seconds) or error. Normal is nearly all success; timeouts mean questions over large date ranges outgrew the database, errors mean a broken query.

panels.title: Funnel run time (p50 and p95)
panels.description: How long a funnel takes to answer. Normal is under a second or two; a p95 near 30 seconds means funnels are about to time out, so look at the brand's event volume and the database's load.

panels.title: Steps of tests in ad networks, by outcome
panels.description: Starting, reading and ending tests inside Google Ads (experiments) and Meta (split tests) per hour, by connector, step and outcome. Normal is success; failed means the network refused (the test shows why); error is retried.

panels.title: Steps of new ads, by outcome
panels.description: Making approved new ads paused, and turning them on, on Google Ads and Meta per hour, by connector, step (create, go_live) and outcome. Normal is success; failed means the platform refused (the draft shows why); error is retried.

panels.title: Refunds sent to ad platforms, by outcome
panels.description: Conversion adjustments: when a payment whose conversion was sent is refunded, its value is restated (partial refund) or the conversion retracted (full refund). Normal: a few sent; skipped means the platform cannot take adjustments (only Google can); failed after retries means the platform kept refusing.

panels.title: AI visibility (ChatGPT and Gemini screens, on workspaces' own answer readers)
AI screen answers, by engine and outcome
panels.description: Answers AI visibility runs read from ChatGPT's and Gemini's own screens through workspaces' own DataForSEO (LLM Scraper), per hour. Normal: mostly done, some budget_reached. connector_unavailable rising means the scraper is failing or changed (alert OutflareAIScreenAnswersFailing): check ai_sample.failed events with provider dataforseo.

panels.title: AI visibility question drafts, by outcome
panels.description: Drafts of AI visibility questions by workspaces' own AI, per hour. Normal: mostly success. ai_failed rising means the AI's answers don't parse or its provider fails: check ai_prompt.draft_failed events by error code.

panels.title: AI visibility demand reads, by kind and outcome
panels.description: Reads of what people ask AI assistants (real questions from DataForSEO's LLM Mentions, AI search volume from its AI keyword data) through workspaces' own connections, per hour. Normal: mostly done; budget_reached is a workspace's own limit. Other outcomes rising mean DataForSEO is failing or changed: check ai_prompt.demand_failed events.

panels.title: AI visibility stance reads, by outcome
panels.description: AI visibility answers read by workspaces' own AI for whether they recommend, list or warn against each brand, per hour. Normal: mostly judged or skipped. ai_failed rising means the reader's answers don't parse: check ai_stance.failed events.

panels.title: Page speed readings, by outcome
panels.description: Page speed readings per minute from visitors' browsers (site.js sends one per page load when the page is left): stored is normal and follows page views; rejected is a reading in the wrong shape or from a site key with no brand; pruned is readings over 90 days old deleted once an hour. Stored near zero while page views flow means the tag is an old copy (before version 16) or data-vitals="off" is set.

panels.title: IP geolocation (DB-IP city and network files)
City and network file age, and downloads
panels.description: How old the DB-IP City Lite and ASN Lite files each server uses are (DB-IP publishes a new month on the 1st, so up to about 31 days is normal), and download attempts in the last 6 hours. not_published is normal for a day or two at the start of a month. A server with no file shows no line: its visits get a country but no region, city or network.

panels.title: Company Telegram accounts, by status
panels.description: Company Telegram accounts signed in to Outflare as a linked device, by status, across workspaces. Normal: almost all connected. signed_out climbs when someone ends Outflare's session from the account's phone or Telegram ends it; failed means a sign-in broke (the steps panel says why).

panels.title: Telegram sign-ins and checks, by step and outcome
panels.description: Sign-in steps (login, password), six-hourly checks and sign-outs per hour, by how they ended. Normal: checks succeed. unreachable means Telegram or the workspace's proxy couldn't be reached; bad_app means Telegram refused a workspace's api_id or api_hash; signed_out means a session ended.

panels.title: Telegram messages synced into the CRM
panels.description: Messages copied from company Telegram accounts into brands' CRMs per hour, received (in) and sent (out). Normal: a burst while an account's history is imported, then a steady trickle in working hours. Zero for hours while accounts are live means the sync stopped (see the runs panel).

panels.title: Telegram syncs, by outcome
panels.description: Syncs of company Telegram accounts per hour, by how they ended. Normal: live (caught up) and importing (copying history). slowed_down means Telegram asked to wait (it carries on by itself); unreachable, signed_out, no_app or bad_app mean an account stopped syncing.

panels.title: Telegram sync lag
panels.description: How long ago the least recently synced company Telegram account finished a sync. Normal: under five minutes (accounts sync every two). Climbing means syncs are failing or the job queue is behind.

panels.title: Telegram chats matched
panels.description: Synced Telegram chats Outflare matched to a customer, by result: confirmed (a record already had its Telegram id), suggested (waits for the account's holder) or no_match. Normal: a burst when an account first syncs, then a trickle. Only no_match for a long time can mean a workspace's AI isn't connected.

panels.title: Telegram chat summaries
panels.description: AI summaries of synced Telegram chats, by outcome: success, no_ai (the workspace has no AI model for Telegram summaries, so nothing is written) or failed (the AI call failed). Normal: mostly success, in bursts when someone asks or an account is handed over.

panels.title: Customers waiting on Telegram
panels.description: Customer chats on company Telegram accounts where the customer wrote last and has waited over four hours (and under three days), across workspaces. Each holder gets a telegram.waiting alert. This is how the team answers, not a fault in Outflare.
